title: The Ten-Million-Year "Drunken Monkey" Mutation — Robert Dudley's Drunken Monkey Hypothesis, Carrigan & Benner's 70-MY Primate ADH4/ADH7 Paleogenetic Resurrection (~10-MYA Ala294Val 40x Ethanol Efficiency Jump Inside PDB 3COS, 1D1S & 1DEH), Bossou Chimpanzees' 51 Palm-Wine Leaf-Sponge Binges & Dunbar–Slingerland Prefrontal Prisoner's Dilemma Math

teenKit.tldr: Forget the myth that alcohol is a 9,000-year-old agricultural accident; our primate ancestors evolved a 40x boost in alcohol-processing power nearly 10 million years ago to sniff out overripe, calorie-packed fruit.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding that our attraction to alcohol is an ancient evolutionary survival tool completely changes how we view human biology, vice, and our deep-rooted relationship with nature.
keyTakeaways: The 'Drunken Monkey Hypothesis' proves that our craving for alcohol isn't a modern glitch, but an ancient adaptation for finding high-calorie fermenting fruit in the wild.

Scientists resurrected ancient proteins in a lab and discovered a single genetic mutation (Ala294Val) from about 10 million years ago that supercharged our ancestors' ability to break down ethanol by 40 times.
Wild primates like chimpanzees and spider monkeys regularly consume ethanol in the wild—from nibbling fermenting fruit to straight-up bingeing on palm-wine left out by humans.

vocab.meaning: Robert Dudley's scientific idea that human fondness for alcohol stems from our tree-dwelling ancestors needing to track down ripe, calorie-dense, fermenting fruit by smell.
A technique where scientists look at ancient DNA sequences and rebuild extinct proteins in a lab to see how they actually functioned millions of years ago.
The massive, 40-fold upgrade in our ancestral enzyme's ability to process alcohol, triggered by a specific single-amino-acid mutation roughly 10 million years ago.
An animal diet that consists primarily of raw fruits, which are naturally sugary and prone to minor alcohol fermentation.

quiz.question: What is the traditional textbook myth about human alcohol consumption that this episode shatters?
options: That humans invented alcohol only 500 years ago during the Industrial Revolution.
Logan, a caveman, accidentally dropped yeast into fruit juice in 12,000 BCE.
That alcohol use is a purely modern, 9,000-year-old agricultural accident caused by farming.
That Neanderthals never drank alcohol because they lacked fermentation vessels.
quiz.explanation: The old narrative claims alcohol was an unnatural intruder introduced only after humans settled down into agriculture.

quiz.question: Approximately how long ago did our primate ancestors experience a 40x jump in ethanol processing efficiency?
quiz.explanation: Paleogenetic resurrection showed that a crucial mutation happened roughly 10 million years ago, long before farming existed.

quiz.question: What genetic and molecular change allowed our ancestors to process alcohol so much faster?
options: The complete loss of the liver organ
A single Ala294Val mutation that supercharged enzyme efficiency inside proteins like PDB 3COS
Eating raw meat instead of fruit
A sudden doubling of stomach size due to cooking
quiz.explanation: A specific amino acid shift (Ala294Val) gave ancient primate ADH enzymes a massive 40x efficiency boost in breaking down ethanol.
